claims.quote: Servicers must comply with applicable law in connection with [their] management of escrow accounts, including collecting, holding, and escrowing funds on behalf of each borrower in accordance with RESPA (12 [U.S.C.] 2609) and Regulation X (12 CFR 1024.17 and 10024.34). . . . Servicers also should ensure compliance with legal requirements regarding the cessation of escrow withholding for [private market insurance] on serviced loans.
claims.summary: Mortgage servicers must comply with RESPA and Regulation X, and ensure compliance with legal requirements regarding the cessation of escrow withholding for private market insurance on serviced loans.

claims.quote: Servicers must closely monitor property taxing authorities and individual insurance contracts to ensure that escrow calculations are accurate and that insurance policies have not lapsed.
claims.summary: Mortgage servicers must closely monitor property taxing authorities and individual insurance contracts to ensure accurate escrow calculations and that insurance policies have not lapsed.

claims.quote: Servicers must comply with applicable law in connection with [their] management of escrow accounts, including collecting, holding, and escrowing funds on behalf of each borrower in accordance with RESPA (12 [U.S.C.] 2609) and Regulation X (12 CFR 1024.17 and 1024.34).
claims.summary: Mortgage servicers must comply with RESPA and Regulation X, including collecting, holding, and escrowing funds on behalf of each borrower.

claims.quote: 12 U.S.C. 1828(o) instructs the Federal banking agencies to ``adopt uniform regulations prescribing standards for extensions of credit'' related to certain real estate transactions.
claims.summary: Federal banking agencies must adopt uniform regulations prescribing standards for extensions of credit related to certain real estate transactions.

claims.quote: 12 U.S.C. 371(a) clearly states that national banks' real estate lending powers are subject both to 12 U.S.C. 1828(o) ``and such restrictions and requirements as the Comptroller of the Currency may prescribe by regulation or order'' (emphasis added).
claims.summary: The Comptroller of the Currency may prescribe restrictions and requirements by regulation or order for national banks' real estate lending powers.

claims.quote: It is a cardinal principle of statutory construction that a statute ought, upon the whole, to be so construed that, if it can be prevented, no clause, sentence, or word shall be superfluous, void, or insignificant.
claims.summary: The Comptroller of the Currency must interpret the statute in a way that ensures no clause, sentence, or word is superfluous, void, or insignificant.

claims.quote:
HOLA provides Federal savings associations broad powers to invest in, sell, or otherwise deal in residential real property loans, subject to regulations issued by the Comptroller.

HOLA also provides the OCC with broad authority to prescribe rules and regulations to provide for the organization, incorporation, examination, operation, and regulation of Federal savings associations and to specify their powers to invest in, sell, or otherwise deal in various loans and other investments.

12 U.S.C. 1464(a); see also Fid. Fed. Sav. & Loan Ass'n v. de la Cuesta, 458 U.S. 141, 145 (1982) (``Pursuant to this authorization [12 U.S.C. 1464(a)], the [Federal Home Loan Bank] Board has promulgated regulations governing the powers and operations of every Federal savings and loan association from its cradle to its corporate grave.'' (citation modified)). This authority to promulgate regulations for Federal savings associations was ultimately transferred to the OCC. 12 U.S.C. 5412(b)(2)(B). The grant of rule writing authority to the OCC in each of 12 U.S.C. 371(a) and 1464(a) is of a type that ``empower[s] an agency to prescribe rules to fill up the details of a statutory scheme . . . or to regulate subject to the limits imposed by a term or phrase that leaves agencies with flexibility . . . .'' Loper Bright Enters. v. Raimondo, 603 U.S. 369, 395 (2024) (citation modified). That is, they are grants of authority to the agency to ``exercise a degree of discretion.'' Id. at 394.
claims.summary: Federal savings associations must comply with regulations issued by the Comptroller regarding residential real property loans and must follow rules and regulations prescribed by the OCC for their operations and powers.

claims.quote: HOLA also authorizes Federal savings associations to engage in nonresidential real estate lending not in excess of 400 percent of capital or certain greater amounts as determined by the Comptroller, subject to regulations issued by the Comptroller. 12 U.S.C. 1464(c)(2)(B).
claims.summary: Federal savings associations must comply with regulations issued by the Comptroller regarding nonresidential real estate lending, which is limited to 400 percent of capital or greater amounts as determined by the Comptroller.

claims.quote: It requires disclosures as to the nature and purposes of escrow accounts,
claims.summary: Lenders must provide disclosures regarding the nature and purposes of escrow accounts.

claims.quote: mandates the provision of free annual escrow account statements,
claims.summary: Lenders must provide free annual escrow account statements.

claims.quote: requires amounts in escrow accounts be paid timely as they become due and any funds remaining in such accounts after the loan is repaid be promptly returned to the borrower,
claims.summary: Lenders must pay amounts in escrow accounts timely as they become due and return any remaining funds to the borrower after the loan is repaid.

claims.quote: establishes proportional caps on the total amounts that may be collected from borrowers in escrow accounts.
claims.summary: Lenders must establish proportional caps on the total amounts that may be collected from borrowers in escrow accounts.

claims.quote: national banks are permitted to engage in the business of banking more generally and ``all such incidental powers as shall be necessary to carry on the business of banking.''
claims.summary: National banks are permitted to engage in the business of banking more generally and all such incidental powers as shall be necessary to carry on the business of banking.

claims.quote: The exercise of the Comptroller's discretion, however, must be kept within reasonable bounds.
claims.summary: The exercise of the Comptroller's discretion must be kept within reasonable bounds.

claims.quote: The OCC considers the following factors when determining whether an activity that is not explicitly enumerated in 12 U.S.C. 24(Seventh) is nonetheless part of the business of banking:
claims.summary: The OCC considers specific factors when determining whether an activity not explicitly enumerated in 12 U.S.C. 24(Seventh) is part of the business of banking.

claims.quote: (i) Whether the activity is the functional equivalent to, or a logical outgrowth of, a recognized banking activity;
claims.summary: The OCC must consider whether the activity is the functional equivalent to, or a logical outgrowth of, a recognized banking activity.

claims.quote: (ii) Whether the activity strengthens the bank by benefiting its customers or its business;
claims.summary: The OCC must consider whether the activity strengthens the bank by benefiting its customers or its business.

claims.quote: (iii) Whether the activity involves risks similar in nature to those already assumed by banks; and
claims.summary: The OCC must consider whether the activity involves risks similar in nature to those already assumed by banks.

claims.quote: (iv) Whether the activity is authorized for State-chartered banks.
claims.summary: The OCC must consider whether the activity is authorized for State-chartered banks.

claims.quote: The weight accorded to each factor depends on the facts and circumstances of each case.
claims.summary: The weight given to each factor in determining whether an activity is incidental to the business of banking depends on the specific facts and circumstances of each case.

claims.quote: An activity is ``incidental to the business of banking if it is convenient or useful to an activity that is specifically authorized for national banks or to an activity that is otherwise part of the business of banking.''
claims.summary: An activity is considered incidental to the business of banking if it is convenient or useful to an authorized activity or part of the business of banking.

claims.quote: The OCC considers the following factors in such analysis: ``(i) Whether the activity facilitates the production or delivery of a bank's products or services, enhances the bank's ability to sell or market its products or services, or improves the effectiveness or efficiency of the bank's operations, in light of risks presented, innovations, strategies, techniques and new technologies for producing and delivering financial products and services; and (ii) Whether the activity enables the bank to use capacity acquired for its banking operations or otherwise avoid economic loss or waste.''
claims.summary: The OCC considers specific factors in determining if an activity is incidental to the business of banking, including whether it facilitates the production or delivery of a bank's products or services and whether it enables the bank to use capacity acquired for its operations or avoid economic loss or waste.

claims.quote: Finally, roughly three quarters of States permit State-chartered banks flexibility to exercise their business judgment as to how to structure the financing of their escrow operations for residential real estate lending, either explicitly SSS or implicitly through silence on the subject,TTT and the OCC is not aware of any State restricting this flexibility with regards to commercial real estate lending.
claims.summary: State-chartered banks have flexibility to structure escrow operations for residential real estate lending, and the OCC is not aware of any State restricting this flexibility for commercial real estate lending.

claims.quote: See Iowa Code sec. 524.905(2) (2025) (``A bank receiving funds in escrow pursuant to an escrow agreement executed in connection with a loan . . . may pay interest to the borrower on those funds.'' (emphasis added)).
claims.summary: State-chartered banks in Iowa may pay interest to the borrower on funds received in escrow pursuant to an escrow agreement executed in connection with a loan.

claims.quote: The States and territories that require their own State-chartered banks to pay specified interest amounts on mortgage-escrow accounts include California (Cal. Civ. Code sec. 2954.8 (2025)), Connecticut (Conn. Gen. Stat. sec. 49-2a (2025)), Guam (11 Guam Code Ann. sec. 106103 (2024)); Maine (Me. Rev. Stat. Ann. tit. 9-B, sec. 429; id. tit. 33, sec. 504), Maryland (Md. Code Ann., Com. Law secs. 12-109, 12-109.2 (2025)), Massachusetts (Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 183, sec. 61 (2025)), Minnesota (Minn. Stat. Ann. sec. 47.20, subd. 9 (2025)), New Hampshire (N.H. Rev. Stat. Ann. sec. 383-B:3-303(a)(7)(E) (2025)), New York (N.Y. Gen. Oblig. Law sec. 5-601 (2025)), Oregon (Or. Rev. Stat. secs. 86.245, 86.250 (2025)), Rhode Island (19 R.I. Gen. Laws sec. 19-9-2 (2025)), U.S. Virgin Islands (V.I. Code tit. 9, sec. 67 2025), Utah (Utah Code Ann. sec. 7-17-3 (2025)), Vermont (Vt. claims.quote: The final rule merely clarifies longstanding and recognized real estate lending powers that banks have exercised under existing law.
claims.summary: The final rule clarifies longstanding and recognized real estate lending powers that banks have exercised under existing law.

claims.quote: This final rule is a permissible exercise of the OCC's congressionally granted authority to clarify national banks' longstanding and recognized real estate lending powers.
claims.summary: The final rule is a permissible exercise of the OCC's congressionally granted authority to clarify national banks' longstanding and recognized real estate lending powers.

claims.quote: the final rule amends the OCC's real estate lending and appraisals regulations applicable to national banks and its lending and investment regulations applicable to Federal savings associations to add a definition of ``escrow account,'' expressly codify banks' power to establish and maintain escrow accounts, and to clarify that the terms and conditions of escrow accounts, including the extent of any compensation paid to customers, are business decisions to be made by each bank.
claims.summary: The final rule amends regulations to add a definition of 'escrow account,' codify banks' power to establish and maintain escrow accounts, and clarify that terms and conditions of escrow accounts are business decisions made by each bank.

claims.quote: the final rule defines an ``escrow account'' used by national banks as an account established in connection with a loan or extension of credit secured by a lien on interest in real estate in which the borrower places funds for the purpose of assuring payment of taxes, insurance premiums, or other charges with respect to the property.
claims.summary: The final rule defines an 'escrow account' as an account established in connection with a loan or extension of credit secured by a lien on interest in real estate, where the borrower places funds for the purpose of assuring payment of taxes, insurance premiums, or other charges.

claims.quote: the final rule defines ``escrow accounts'' in substantially similar terms in the context of Federal savings associations.
claims.summary: The final rule defines 'escrow accounts' in substantially similar terms in the context of Federal savings associations.

claims.quote: the final rule codifies national banks' escrow powers, including the flexibility such banks have as to how to organize and manage escrow accounts.
claims.summary: The final rule codifies national banks' escrow powers, including the flexibility such banks have as to how to organize and manage escrow accounts.

claims.quote: the final rule codifies that (1) the powers of national banks include establishing and maintaining escrow accounts in connection with real estate loans; and (2) the terms and conditions of such escrow accounts (including, but not limited to, the investment of escrowed funds, fees assessed for the provision of such accounts, and whether and to what extent interest or other compensation is calculated and paid to customers whose funds are placed in the escrow account) are business decisions to be made by each national bank in its discretion.
claims.summary: The final rule codifies that national banks have the power to establish and maintain escrow accounts in connection with real estate loans, and that the terms and conditions of such accounts are business decisions to be made by each national bank in its discretion.

claims.quote: the final rule codifies these powers in the context of Federal savings associations in substantially similar terms.
claims.summary: The final rule codifies these powers in the context of Federal savings associations in substantially similar terms.

claims.quote: The OCC remains committed to ensuring that homeowners' escrow funds are protected against abusive practices.
claims.summary: The OCC remains committed to ensuring that homeowners' escrow funds are protected against abusive practices.

claims.quote: prohibiting unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce
claims.summary: Prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce.

claims.quote: requiring national banks to adopt and maintain written policies that establish appropriate limits and standards for real estate lending, including that they be consistent with safe and sound banking practices
claims.summary: Require national banks to adopt and maintain written policies for real estate lending that are consistent with safe and sound banking practices.

claims.quote: requiring banks to establish loan administration procedures that address escrow account administration
claims.summary: Require banks to establish loan administration procedures that address escrow account administration.

claims.quote: no agency may conduct or sponsor, nor is the respondent required to respond to, an information collection unless it displays a currently valid Office of Management and Budget (OMB) control number
claims.summary: Prohibits an agency from conducting or sponsoring, and the respondent from responding to, an information collection unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number.

claims.quote: this analysis is not required if an agency certifies that the rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities and publishes its certification and a short explanatory statement in the Federal Register along with its rule
claims.summary: Requires an agency to certify that a rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities and to publish the certification and a short explanatory statement in the Federal Register.

claims.quote: the OCC classifies the economic impact on an individual small entity as significant if the total estimated impact in one year is greater than 5 percent of the small entity's total annual salaries and benefits or greater than 2.5 percent of the small entity's total non-interest expense.
claims.summary: The OCC classifies the economic impact on an individual small entity as significant based on specific thresholds.

claims.quote: the OCC considers 5 percent or more of OCC-supervised small entities to be a substantial number, and at present, 30 OCC-supervised small entities would constitute a substantial number.
claims.summary: The OCC considers 5 percent or more of OCC-supervised small entities to be a substantial number, with 30 entities currently being considered substantial.

claims.quote: the OCC certifies that the final rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities supervised by the OCC.
claims.summary: The OCC certifies that the final rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.

claims.quote: the OCC has analyzed the final rule under the factors in the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (UMRA).
claims.summary: The OCC has analyzed the final rule under the factors in the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995.

claims.quote: the OCC considers whether the final rule includes a Federal mandate that may result in the expenditure by State, local, and tribal governments, in the aggregate, or by the private sector, of $100 million or more in any one year ($193 million as adjusted annually for inflation).
claims.summary: The OCC considers whether the final rule includes a Federal mandate that may result in the expenditure by State, local, and tribal governments, in the aggregate, or by the private sector, of $100 million or more in any one year.

claims.quote: the OCC has not prepared the written statement described in section 202 of the UMRA.
claims.summary: The OCC has not prepared the written statement described in section 202 of the UMRA.

claims.quote: the OCC must consider, consistent with principles of safety and soundness and the public interest, (1) any administrative burdens that the final rule would place on depository institutions, including small depository institutions and customers of depository institutions and (2) the benefits of the final rule.
claims.summary: The OCC must consider administrative burdens and benefits of the final rule on depository institutions and customers.

claims.quote: This rulemaking will not impose any reporting, disclosure, or other requirements on insured depository institutions.
claims.summary: This rulemaking will not impose any reporting, disclosure, or other requirements on insured depository institutions.

claims.quote: Executive Order 12866, titled ``Regulatory Planning and Review,'' as amended, requires the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA), OMB, to determine whether a final rule is a ``significant regulatory action'' prior to the disclosure of the final rule to the public.
claims.affected_party: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA), OMB
claims.summary: Determine if a final rule is a significant regulatory action prior to disclosure to the public.

claims.quote: If OIRA finds the final rule to be a ``significant regulatory action,'' Executive Order 12866 requires the OCC to conduct a cost-benefit analysis of the final rule and for OIRA to conduct a review of the final rule prior to publication in the Federal Register.
claims.summary: Conduct a cost-benefit analysis and review of the final rule prior to publication in the Federal Register if it is a significant regulatory action.

claims.quote: Executive Order 14192, titled ``Unleashing Prosperity Through Deregulation,'' requires that an agency, unless prohibited by law, identify at least 10 existing regulations to be repealed when the agency publicly proposes for notice and comment or otherwise promulgates a new regulation with total costs greater than zero.
claims.summary: Identify at least 10 existing regulations to be repealed when proposing or promulgating a new regulation with total costs greater than zero.

claims.quote: Executive Order 14192 further requires that new incremental costs associated with new regulations shall, to the extent permitted by law, be offset by the elimination of existing costs associated with at least 10 prior regulations.
claims.summary: Offset new incremental costs associated with new regulations by eliminating existing costs from at least 10 prior regulations.

claims.quote: For purposes of the Congressional Review Act, OMB makes a determination as to whether a final rule constitutes a ``major'' rule.
claims.summary: Determine whether a final rule constitutes a major rule under the Congressional Review Act.

claims.quote: If a rule is deemed a ``major rule'' by the OMB, the Congressional Review Act generally provides that the rule may not take effect until at least 60 days following its publication.
claims.summary: A major rule may not take effect until at least 60 days following its publication.

claims.quote: the OCC will submit the final rule and other appropriate reports to Congress and the Government Accountability Office for review.
claims.summary: The OCC must submit the final rule and other appropriate reports to Congress and the Government Accountability Office for review.

claims.summary: Federal savings associations may establish or maintain escrow accounts, and the terms and conditions of such accounts are business decisions to be made by each association in its discretion.
